entries.title: Ezekiel 19:1
segments: When we compare the weakness and helpless dependence of the royal family of Judah in the days of Jeremiah and Ezekiel, with its glory and strength in the time of David and Solomon, we have an affecting proof of God's supreme power over nations, as well as of his unalterable determination to destroy every people that persists in transgressing his laws.

entries.title: Ezekiel 19:2
segments:
Thy mother; Jerusalem, as representing the Jewish state; the address is to Israel in the general sense, not to the ten tribes alone, as distinct from the two. 
 
  A lioness; compare

entries.title: Ezekiel 19:3
segments: One of her whelps; Jehoahaz, whom Pharaoh-necho deposed and carried into Egypt.

entries.title: Ezekiel 19:5
segments: Another of her whelps; the three kings who succeeded Jehoahaz were all carried to Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar.  Of these some understand here Jehoiakim, as the immediate successor of Jehoahaz; others Jehoiachin, because he alone of the three was raised to the throne by the people.  But probably the fate of this second whelp represents that of "the princes of Israel" generally after Jehoahaz.

entries.title: Ezekiel 19:10
segments:
Is like a vine; or, "was like a vine," propserous and flourishing. 
 
  In thy blood; in thy vigor and strength.  The prophet here repeats what he has just said, under a new image.

entries.title: Ezekiel 19:14
segments: Out of a rod of her branches; Zedekiah's rebvellion against the king of Babylon became a consuming fire, which destroyed his kingdom and "the princes of Israel" together.
